# VoIP Multi-Network Laboratory

This case study documents a hands-on VoIP learning environment designed for vocational telecommunications education.

The laboratory uses a multi-network architecture in which each student builds and manages an independent VoIP network while a central instructor-managed infrastructure provides shared provider and interconnection services.

Each student works with a dedicated router, laptop, virtual PBX environment, physical IP telephone, and softphone endpoints. This allows students to configure and troubleshoot a complete VoIP system rather than interacting only with a preconfigured centralized PBX.

## Learning Environment

The laboratory integrates practical concepts including IPv4 addressing, LAN/WAN segmentation, routing, NAT, virtualized PBX deployment, SIP extensions, physical and software endpoints, SIP trunks, call routing, PBX services, port forwarding, and analog/VoIP interoperability.

## Layered Network Model

- **School / Enterprise Network:** `10.0.0.0/8`
- **VoIP Laboratory / Provider Network:** `172.16.0.0/16`
- **Student / Customer LAN:** `192.168.1.0/24`

Each student router connects its WAN interface to the shared laboratory/provider network while creating an isolated private LAN for the student's PBX and VoIP endpoints.

## Student Laboratory Environment

Each student operates a complete routed VoIP environment using a laptop, dedicated router, physical SIP/IP telephone, VirtualBox PBX, laptop softphone, and mobile softphone endpoint.

## Progressive Learning Sequence

The Module 21 laboratory sequence develops the system progressively from virtualization and PBX installation through SIP endpoints, trunking, inbound/outbound routing, recordings, announcements, ring groups, queues, time-based routing, and IVR.

The result is a functioning student-managed telephone system in which later activities depend on services configured during earlier activities.

[**Explore the Module 21 Learning Activities →**](learning-activities/index.qmd)

## Central VoIP Infrastructure

A separate instructor-managed mobile platform provides the shared provider/interconnection network through a Linux/FreePBX/Asterisk server, Ethernet switching, routing infrastructure, and SIP testing endpoint.

## Advanced Connectivity

After the individual systems are operational, students explore NAT and port forwarding by allowing an endpoint on another network to register to an extension hosted on their PBX.

## Cross-Module Integration

When the same cohort completes both the Analog Telephony and VoIP modules, the two laboratory environments can be interconnected through a SIP trunk. The instructional roles are intentionally reversed: analog infrastructure is tested through VoIP in the Analog module, while VoIP infrastructure can reach analog endpoints in the VoIP module.
